title: Nicholas Giardina
text:
I am an archaeology graduate and research assistant working at the intersection of archaeological research, structured data, spatial analysis, and visual communication.
This portfolio presents selected work in ethnographic data production, interactive visualization in R, archaeological mapping in QGIS, and archaeological illustration in Adobe Illustrator.

title: Nicholas Giardina
text:
Selected work

Ethnographic Fire-Use Dataset
A structured and model-oriented dataset developed from ethnographic literature concerning Indigenous fire practices in northern Alberta.
View the dataset project


Interactive Data Visualizations
Interactive figures developed in R to communicate the dataset’s classification, evidence relationships, spatial forms, and timing patterns.
View the interactive visualizations


Archaeological Mapping
Regional and close-up maps created in QGIS to communicate source locations, cultural landscapes, and archaeological features.
View the mapping work


Archaeological Illustration
Vector illustrations of archaeological sites and structural features in Greenland, created from field documentation in Adobe Illustrator.
View the illustrations

title: Ethnographic Fire-Use Dataset
text:
Database Design and Research Workflow
This figure summarizes how source material was transformed into a structured and reviewable database. It distinguishes source material, LLM-assisted processing, human supervision, and resulting database outputs. The second panel shows the relationships and purposes of the Version 2.0 workbook tables.




Dataset: Fire-use database Version 2.0, developed by Matthew Walls and Nicholas Giardina. Figure: Nicholas Giardina.


Open full-size figure
Download PDF

My role: I helped develop, clean, and validate the relational database and produced this figure in R to communicate its workflow and table structure.
Skills demonstrated: Relational data organization, evidence traceability, data quality control, responsible use of LLM-assisted methods, workflow documentation, and technical visualization.

title: Ethnographic Fire-Use Dataset
text:
Model-Facing Data Architecture
The Modeling Crosswalk translates 51 source-traceable canonical fire uses into qualitative descriptors that can support comparative research and responsible model development. The figure organizes those descriptors into practice, space and time, expected fire behaviour, ecological response, and evidence and reuse.




Source: Fire-use database Version 2.0. Figure: Nicholas Giardina.


Open full-size figure
Download PDF

My role: I helped structure and validate the model-facing variables and created this figure to explain how evidence-based cultural information is translated into cautious qualitative modeling descriptors.
Skills demonstrated: Data modeling, variable design, qualitative data transformation, research communication, visual hierarchy, and responsible model-use documentation.

title: Ethnographic Fire-Use Dataset
text:
Worked Crosswalk Example
This worked example shows how one canonical fire-use record is represented in the Modeling Crosswalk. CFU-007 is supported by five sources, six source units, and 47 linked claims.




Record: CFU-007, Moose-browse and hunting-site burning. Source: Fire-use database Version 2.0. Figure: Nicholas Giardina.

title: Mapping
text:
This regional map situates the communities, ethnographic source locations, contextual places, waterways, and administrative boundaries relevant to the northern Alberta fire-use research.


CRS: NAD83(CSRS) / Alberta 10-TM (Forest) (EPSG:3402).
Sources: Government of Alberta / Alberta Data Partnerships Ltd. (reserve boundaries); Parks Canada (Wood Buffalo National Park boundary); Natural Resources Canada, Canada3D (elevation and derived hillshade); © OpenStreetMap contributors (Alberta boundary, rivers, and lakes), ODbL. Source and contextual locations compiled by Matthew Walls primarily from project source literature. Cartography by Nicholas Giardina.


Open full-size map
Download credited PDF

My role: I designed and produced this map in QGIS to communicate the geographic context of the ethnographic fire-use dataset.
Skills demonstrated: Coordinate reference system management, spatial data organization, cartographic hierarchy, symbology, labeling, print-layout design, and export preparation.
Design approach: Places directly associated with the source material are visually distinguished from broader contextual locations and boundaries. The map balances regional orientation with the visibility of communities, waterways, and the Wood Buffalo National Park context.

title: Mapping
text:
Meander River Close-Up Map
This close-up map provides more detailed geographic context for Meander River and the surrounding landscape discussed in the research sources.


CRS: NAD83(CSRS) / Alberta 10-TM (Forest) (EPSG:3402).
Sources: Government of Alberta / Alberta Data Partnerships Ltd. (reserve boundary); © OpenStreetMap contributors (rivers), ODbL. Imagery: Esri World Imagery, Vantor WorldView-3 (WV03), acquired 17 June 2025. Source and contextual locations compiled by Matthew Walls primarily from project source literature. Cartography by Nicholas Giardina.


Open full-size map
Download credited PDF

My role: I designed this close-up map in QGIS to complement the regional map with a more localized view.
Skills demonstrated: Multi-scale cartographic design, basemap integration, hydrology display, label placement, visual hierarchy, and print-layout production.
Design approach: The map retains enough surrounding landscape context to orient the viewer while focusing attention on Meander River and the locally relevant features.
